text: What is the loudest animal on Earth? Not a lion. Not a blue whale.
Its giant square head is mostly nose. The biggest nose of any animal.
Inside, it pushes air past a pair of flaps nicknamed monkey lips, and fires clicks into the dark.
It uses them like sonar, to find squid a thousand meters down.
In 2003, scientists measured clicks of up to two hundred thirty six decibels, underwater.
By far the loudest sound ever recorded from any animal.
Careful: decibels underwater aren't the same as decibels in air.
Converted to air, it's still around one hundred seventy four. Far louder than a rock concert.
And other sperm whales can hear those clicks tens of kilometers away.
Verdict: solved. The loudest animal on Earth.
Using that voice to hunt, in total darkness.
